Computing the first derivative, we get \[ \begin{align} \dfrac {\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x} & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(3x^5 + 4x^3 - 10x^2\right) \\ & = 5\cdot 3x^4 + 3\cdot 4x^2 - 2 \cdot 10x \\ & = 15x^4 + 12x^2 - 20x \,.\\ \end{align} \]

Computing the second derivative, we get \[ \begin{align} \dfrac {\textrm{d}^2y}{\textrm{d}x^2} & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left (15x^4 + 12x^2 - 20x\right ) \\ & = 15\cdot 4x^3 + 2\cdot 12x -20 \\ & =60x^3 + 24x -20. \\ \end{align} \]

Computing the first derivative, we get

\[ \begin{align} \dfrac {\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x} & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(3x^3 - 8x\right) \\[5pt] & = 3\cdot 3x^2 - 8 \\[5pt] & = 9x^2 - 8 . \end{align} \]

Computing the second derivative, we get \[ \begin{align} \dfrac {\textrm{d}^2y}{\textrm{d}x^2} & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left (9x^2 - 8\right ) \\[5pt] & = 2\cdot 9x \\[5pt] & =\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{18x}. \end{align} \]

question.explanation:
Computing the first derivative, we get \[ \begin{align} \dfrac {\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x} & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left( \dfrac{x^8}{4} +x - \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{x}}\right) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left( \dfrac{x^8}{4} +x - {4}{x^{-1/2}}\right) \\[5pt] & = 8\cdot \dfrac{x^7}4 +1 - \left(-\dfrac12\right)\cdot 4 x^{-3/2} \\[5pt] & = 2x^7 +1 + 2x^{-3/2} . \end{align} \]

Computing the second derivative, we get \[ \begin{align} \dfrac {\textrm{d}^2y}{\textrm{d}x^2} & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left (2x^7 +1 + 2x^{-3/2} \right ) \\[5pt] & = 7\cdot 2x^6 + 0 + \left(-\dfrac32\right)\cdot 2x^{-5/2} \\[5pt] & = 14x^6 - 3x^{-5/2} \\[5pt] & =\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{14x^6 - \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{x^5}}}. \end{align} \]

example.title: Computing Second Order Derivatives Using Leibniz Notation

question.explanation:
First, notice that we can rewrite the function as follows:

\begin{align} f(x) &= \dfrac{x^5-x^2+x}{4x^2}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{x^3}{4} - \dfrac{1}{4}+\dfrac{1}{4x} \end{align}

Now, computing the first derivative, we get \begin{align} f'(x) &= \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left( \dfrac{x^3}{4} - \dfrac{1}{4}+\dfrac{1}{4x} \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left( \dfrac{x^3}{4} - \dfrac{1}{4}+\dfrac{1}{4} x^{-1} \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3x^2}{4} - \dfrac{1 }{4}x^{-2} . \end{align}

Computing the second derivative, we get \begin{align} f''(x) &= \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left( \dfrac{3x^2}{4} - \dfrac{1 }{4}x^{-2}\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3x}{2}+\dfrac{1}{2}x^{-3} . \end{align}

Finally, computing the third derivative, we get \begin{align} f'''(x) &= \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(\dfrac{3x}{2}+\dfrac{1}{2}x^{-3}\right) \\[5pt] &=\dfrac32-\dfrac32x^{-4} \\[5pt] & =\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{3}{2}-\dfrac{3}{2x^4}}. \end{align}
